Track the sedimentation rate through an eCOCO map

Source: R/track_ecoco.R
track_ecoco.Rd

Interactively select points in the map of an eCOCO result (sedimentation rate against depth) to trace how the sedimentation rate changes along the record. This is the eCOCO counterpart of track_period: the map of one of the eCOCO statistics (by default the combined correlation and significance score pcoco) is plotted, the local maxima (ridges) are marked, and the sedimentation rate is tracked by clicking ridge points.

Selected points are shown as white dots. Clicking a selected point again deselects it (red dot). Press the right mouse button or Esc (depending on the graphics device) to finish. An interactive device that supports identify is needed (on Windows this works out of the box, on macOS XQuartz or the Quartz device, on Linux an X11 device).

The tracking can also be done without a mouse: pass the points as points. They are snapped to the nearest ridge point, which makes a tracking reproducible and scriptable.

Usage

track_ecoco(
  ecoco = NULL,
  map = c("pcoco", "rho", "score", "p_global", "norbit"),
  track_peaks = TRUE,
  n_peaks = 3,
  rho_min = NULL,
  p_max = NULL,
  norbit_min = NULL,
  points = NULL,
  interpolate = FALSE,
  n.levels = 100,
  plot_horizontal = TRUE,
  plot_dir = TRUE,
  x_lab = "depth (metres)",
  y_lab = "sedimentation rate (cm/kyr)",
  palette_name = "viridis",
  genplot = FALSE
)

Arguments

ecoco

eCOCO result to track (required): the list returned by ecoco_adaptive, ecoco_blocked or ecoco_interleaved, with the vectors sr (sedimentation rates, cm/kyr) and depth (window centres) and rate-by-window matrices (one row per rate, one column per window). Default=NULL.

map

The eCOCO statistic used for tracking and plotting (character): "pcoco" (combined correlation and significance score), "rho" (correlation coefficient), "score", "p_global" (global p-value, shown and tracked as minus log10 p) or "norbit" (number of contributing orbital periods); it must be present in ecoco. Default=c("pcoco", "rho", "score", "p_global", "norbit"), i.e. "pcoco".

track_peaks

Only allow the local maxima of the map along the sedimentation rate axis to be selected (logical); FALSE allows every grid cell. Default=TRUE.

n_peaks

Maximum number of peaks per window that can be selected, the highest ones (integer, > 0; Inf keeps all); only used with track_peaks = TRUE. Default=3.

rho_min

Minimum correlation coefficient (rho of ecoco) a point must have to be selectable (numeric, or NULL for no criterion). Default=NULL.

p_max

Maximum global p-value (p_global of ecoco) a point may have to be selectable (numeric, between 0 and 1, or NULL for no criterion). Default=NULL.

norbit_min

Minimum number of contributing orbital periods (norbit of ecoco) a point must have to be selectable (integer, or NULL for no criterion). Default=NULL.

points

Points to select without mouse input (data frame or matrix with depth in column 1 and sedimentation rate in cm/kyr in column 2, or NULL for interactive selection). Each point is snapped to the nearest selectable point (distance scaled by the ranges of depth and rate). Default=NULL.

interpolate

Linearly interpolate the tracked sedimentation rate to all windows of the eCOCO result, constant outside the tracked interval (logical); the result then only has the columns depth and sedrate. Default=FALSE.

n.levels

Number of colour levels of the map (integer, > 1); the breaks are evenly spaced. Default=100.

plot_horizontal

Orientation of the map (logical): depth on the x-axis (TRUE) or on the y-axis (FALSE). Default=TRUE.

plot_dir

Direction of the depth axis (logical): TRUE draws depth increasing along the axis, FALSE reverses it (for example for borehole data with depth increasing downwards). Default=TRUE.

x_lab

Label of the depth axis (character). Default="depth (metres)".

y_lab

Label of the sedimentation rate axis (character). Default="sedimentation rate (cm/kyr)".

palette_name

Name of a hcl.colors palette for the colour scale, a character string, for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1"; run grDevices::hcl.pals() to list all 115 names. Low values get the first colour of the palette. Names of the viridis family ("viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo") give the colours of the viridis package, as in the wavelet plots. Default="viridis".

genplot

Plot the map with the selected points and the tracked curve when points is used (logical); the interactive mode always plots. Default=FALSE.

Value

A data frame with the tracked windows: depth, sedrate (cm/kyr) and, when available in ecoco, rho, p_global, norbit and the value of the map. The result can be used like the output of track_period (for example to build an age model).

See also

ecoco_track, ecoco_track_ridge, track_period

Author

Michiel Arts. Inspired by track_period and the tracking routines of Acycle (Mingsong Li); see ecoco_track for the automatic version.

Examples

# synthetic eCOCO-like map: sedimentation rate increases with depth
sr <- seq(1, 10, by = 0.25)
depth <- seq(0, 20, by = 0.5)
true_sr <- 4 + 2 * depth / 20
rho <- 0.8 * exp(-outer(sr, true_sr, "-")^2 / 0.5)
ecoco <- list(sr = sr, depth = depth, rho = rho, pcoco = 2 * rho,
              p_global = matrix(0.01, length(sr), length(depth)),
              norbit = matrix(9, length(sr), length(depth)))
# scripted tracking: points are snapped to the nearest ridge point
trk <- track_ecoco(ecoco, points = data.frame(depth = c(2, 10, 18), sr = c(4.2, 5, 5.8)))
trk
#>   depth sedrate     rho p_global norbit   pcoco
#> 1     2    4.25 0.79601     0.01      9 1.59202
#> 2    10    5.00 0.80000     0.01      9 1.60000
#> 3    18    5.75 0.79601     0.01      9 1.59202
# \donttest{
# interactive tracking (needs a graphics device with mouse input)
if (interactive()) {
  trk <- track_ecoco(ecoco)
}
# }
